## Appearance

Leslie Moore is described as extraordinarily lovely, possessing striking good looks and arms that gleam like ivory-tinted marble. Her most prominent feature is her beautiful, splendid hair that gleams like molten gold and falls to her feet in a fountain of living gold, giving her the appearance of being golden-crowned. She has sea-blue eyes filled with soft laughter and allurement, as well as slender, brown, work-hardened hands. She wears a plain dress of cheap, cream-tinted cotton voile paired with a crimson girdle.

_Sources: [v4 CHAPTER 10 LESLIE MOORE P28](../source/v04-c10.md#nw-v04-c10-p0028), [v4 CHAPTER 12 LESLIE COMES OVER P5](../source/v04-c12.md#nw-v04-c12-p0005), [v4 CHAPTER 21 BARRIERS SWEPT AWAY P17](../source/v04-c21.md#nw-v04-c21-p0017), [v4 CHAPTER 23 OWEN FORD COMES P24](../source/v04-c23.md#nw-v04-c23-p0024), [v4 CHAPTER 26 OWEN FORD’S CONFESSION P18](../source/v04-c26.md#nw-v04-c26-p0018), [v4 CHAPTER 33 LESLIE RETURNS P14](../source/v04-c33.md#nw-v04-c33-p0014), +3 more_

## Personality

Leslie Moore possesses a clever, glowing, and pent-up personality, driven by a strong sense of duty despite her lingering unhappiness. Possessing a resolute nature, she dislikes being pitied and acts protectively when taking her husband around strangers. More recently, a notable change has come over her, leaving her laughing and cheerful. Gifted in dancing and exquisite handwork such as delicate embroidery, her ambitions include working to make money to shingle her roof, wishing to be a mother, and intending to move to [Montreal](../codex/places.md#montreal) to pursue nursing.

_Sources: [v4 CHAPTER 15 CHRISTMAS AT FOUR WINDS P6](../source/v04-c15.md#nw-v04-c15-p0006), [v4 CHAPTER 16 NEW YEAR’S EVE AT THE LIGHT P11](../source/v04-c16.md#nw-v04-c16-p0011), [v4 CHAPTER 17 A FOUR WINDS WINTER P10](../source/v04-c17.md#nw-v04-c17-p0010), [v4 CHAPTER 17 A FOUR WINDS WINTER P12](../source/v04-c17.md#nw-v04-c17-p0012), [v4 CHAPTER 19 DAWN AND DUSK P28](../source/v04-c19.md#nw-v04-c19-p0028), [v4 CHAPTER 22 MISS CORNELIA ARRANGES MATTERS P24](../source/v04-c22.md#nw-v04-c22-p0024), +7 more_

## History

The daughter of [Frank West](../character/frank-west.md) and Rose Elliott, Leslie Moore experienced a tragic youth, finding her father after he committed suicide when she was fourteen, and losing her four-year-younger brother [Kenneth](../character/kenneth.md) to a farm accident when she was twelve. Coerced into marrying [Dick Moore](../character/dick-moore.md) at sixteen to save her mother's home from mortgage foreclosure, Leslie subsequently lost her mother to pneumonia the following spring. Despite her difficult circumstances, she inherited money from her grandmother [West](../character/west.md) to attend Queen's [Academy](../codex/places.md#queen-s-academy), where she completed two years of coursework in a single year to earn her First, before returning home to teach at the [Glen](../codex/places.md#glen) school. Leslie formed a friendship with [Anne](../character/anne-shirley.md) [Blythe](../character/blythe.md) at [Four Winds](../codex/places.md#four-winds), eventually confessing to [Anne](../character/anne-shirley.md) that she had initially felt intense envy and resentment toward her happiness before the two reconciled. When writer [Owen Ford](../character/owen-ford.md) stayed at her home as a boarder while adapting Captain Jim's life story into a novel, Leslie developed deep feelings for him and tearfully confessed her love to [Anne](../character/anne-shirley.md) when he departed. [Gilbert Blythe](../character/gilbert-blythe.md) later informed Leslie of a potential medical operation for [Dick](../character/dick-moore.md); she secured a mortgage from Captain Jim to take him to [Montreal](../codex/places.md#montreal), where the surgery revealed that the man was actually Dick's lookalike cousin, [George Moore](../character/george-moore.md), and that her husband had died years prior. Freed from her marriage, Leslie stayed with [Anne](../character/anne-shirley.md) and [Gilbert](../character/gilbert-blythe.md) when Owen returned to [Four Winds](../codex/places.md#four-winds), leading Owen to declare his love for her, which she eagerly returned. Afterward, Leslie comforted [Anne](../character/anne-shirley.md) during her move to the [Glen](../codex/places.md#glen) by sharing that Owen planned to purchase the house of dreams as a summer home.

_Sources: [v4 CHAPTER 10 LESLIE MOORE P4](../source/v04-c10.md#nw-v04-c10-p0004), [v4 CHAPTER 10 LESLIE MOORE P10](../source/v04-c10.md#nw-v04-c10-p0010), [v4 CHAPTER 10 LESLIE MOORE P28](../source/v04-c10.md#nw-v04-c10-p0028), [v4 CHAPTER 10 LESLIE MOORE P49](../source/v04-c10.md#nw-v04-c10-p0049), [v4 CHAPTER 10 LESLIE MOORE P58](../source/v04-c10.md#nw-v04-c10-p0058), [v4 CHAPTER 11 THE STORY OF LESLIE MOORE P15](../source/v04-c11.md#nw-v04-c11-p0015), +41 more_

## Quotes

> “I ENVY Anne,” said Leslie suddenly and fiercely, “and I’d envy her even if she had died! She was a mother for one beautiful day. I’d gladly give my life for THAT!”
>
> — Leslie Moore — [v4 CHAPTER 19 DAWN AND DUSK P28](../source/v04-c19.md#nw-v04-c19-p0028)

> "If I had known I would have gone away—I wouldn’t have stayed here to meet him. You should have told me. It wasn’t fair of you, Anne—oh, it wasn’t fair!"
>
> — Leslie Moore — [v4 CHAPTER 36 BEAUTY FOR ASHES P47](../source/v04-c36.md#nw-v04-c36-p0047)

> "Anne likes the pink ones best, and Gilbert likes the white. But I want the crimson ones. They satisfy some craving in me as no other flower does."
>
> — Leslie Moore — [v4 CHAPTER 38 RED ROSES P5](../source/v04-c38.md#nw-v04-c38-p0005)

> "It seems too great to be real—I’m afraid to speak of it—to think of it. It seems to me that it must just be another dream of this house of dreams and it will vanish when I leave here."
>
> — Leslie Moore — [v4 CHAPTER 38 RED ROSES P29](../source/v04-c38.md#nw-v04-c38-p0029)

> "And, oh! I have such good news. He writes me that he is going to buy this place from the church trustees and keep it to spend our summer vacations in. Anne, are you not glad?"
>
> — Leslie Moore — [v4 CHAPTER 40 FAREWELL TO THE HOUSE OF DREAMS P56](../source/v04-c40.md#nw-v04-c40-p0056)

## Relationships

### [Anne Shirley](../character/anne-shirley.md) · [the relationship](../relationships/anne-shirley--leslie-moore.md)

[Anne Shirley](../character/anne-shirley.md) and Leslie Moore began their relationship as coastal neighbors who met while walking along the shore and agreed to become friends despite Leslie's reserved, troubled nature [R2, S1]. They grew into close companions who shared intimate fireside conversations, autumn walks to the lighthouse, and social visits [R1, S2, S4, S5]. Despite lingering bitterness and unspoken emotional barriers from Leslie regarding the contrast in their lives, their bond deepened after Leslie gifted [Anne](../character/anne-shirley.md) a handcrafted baby dress and later stayed with Anne's family [S2, S6, S28].

_Sources: [v4 CHAPTER 10 LESLIE MOORE P4](../source/v04-c10.md#nw-v04-c10-p0004), [v4 CHAPTER 10 LESLIE MOORE P10](../source/v04-c10.md#nw-v04-c10-p0010), [v4 CHAPTER 10 LESLIE MOORE P28](../source/v04-c10.md#nw-v04-c10-p0028), +34 more_

### [Dick Moore](../character/dick-moore.md) · [the relationship](../relationships/dick-moore--leslie-moore.md)

[Dick Moore](../character/dick-moore.md) was believed to be Leslie's husband, whom she cared for and arranged to send to [Montreal](../codex/places.md#montreal) for brain surgery with medical and financial assistance [R5, S10, S11]. However, a letter from Leslie revealed that the real [Dick Moore](../character/dick-moore.md) had actually died years prior, and the man living in her household was in fact his lookalike cousin, [George Moore](../character/george-moore.md) [S11].
